take: What we like about Manors is that it argued itself into a corner and then built its way out. The 2019 pitch from Jojo Regan and Luke Davies was that the industry was solving a problem they did not have — they had spent a summer playing in clothes that were nothing like golf clothes and been fine. Seven years on the rack holds Polartec polos and recycled technical trousers, which ought to be a climbdown and instead reads as the brand growing up without changing its mind about how things should look.
The Outsider Polartec® Polo at $115 is where you see it: modern fabric cut to a silhouette Nick Watts pointed at golf’s golden age, so it performs like this decade and photographs like 1968.
It suits the player who wants the Palmer-era line without vintage-era sizing, and who would rather the clothes carry into the afternoon. Entry is $68; the collab racks run to $284.
story_extra: Manors is a London golf label founded in 2019 by two school friends who could not find clothes they wanted to play in. Seven years on it sells Polartec polos, recycled technical trousers and quarter-zip mid-layers — which is remarkable mainly because the brand was built on the argument that none of that matters.

The founding pitch was explicit. Jojo Regan and Luke Davies had been playing together through the summer of 2018 dressed nothing like golfers, and concluded that the industry was solving a problem they did not have. Nick Watts joined as Fashion Director and pointed the aesthetic at golf’s golden age — Palmer, Player, Nicklaus — under a line the brand still uses: personality before performance.

The brand went dark on social in spring 2023 and came back as a technical golf brand. What follows is who they were, what changed, the three collaborations that mark the arc, and what is actually hanging on the rail now — because the most interesting thing about the current range is that both halves of the argument are still on it.
